create.name: Matthieu Ricard
create.bio:
Matthieu Ricard is a French Buddhist monk, writer, translator and photographer. Born in 1946 to the philosopher Jean-François Revel and the painter Yahne Le Toumelin, he first travelled to India in 1967 and met Tibetan masters there. He completed a doctorate in cell genetics in 1972 and then left science behind to settle in the Himalayas, where he has lived ever since, and since 1989 he has been the Dalai Lama's French interpreter.

He is best known for his books on happiness, altruism and meditation, which bring Buddhist practice into conversation with modern research; they include Happiness, Altruism, Why Meditate? and The Monk and the Philosopher, a set of conversations with his father. As a member of the Mind and Life Institute he has taken part in university studies of how meditation affects the brain, and his TED talks on happiness and altruism have reached millions. He has also translated many Tibetan texts, among them The Life of Shabkar, and published photo books of Himalayan landscapes and people. All income from his books, photographs and events goes to Karuna-Shechen, the humanitarian organisation he set up to run education, health and social projects in the Himalayan region. He is clear that he doesn't see himself as a teacher, and he points people to his writing rather than giving teachings.

books.title: Happiness: A Guide to Developing Life's Most Important Skill
books.author: Matthieu Ricard
books.description: Drawing on Buddhist practice and his scientific training, Ricard argues that lasting happiness is a skill built from inner conditions, and shows how to cultivate them.

books.title: Altruism: The Power of Compassion to Change Yourself and the World
books.author: Matthieu Ricard
books.description: A long, wide-ranging case for altruism as something that benefits both the giver and society, built on decades of his own practice and on research.

books.title: Why Meditate: Working with Thoughts and Emotions
books.author: Matthieu Ricard
books.description: A short guide answering why to meditate, on what and how, with practical exercises for working with thoughts and emotions.

books.title: The Monk and the Philosopher: A Father and Son Discuss the Meaning of Life
books.author: Jean-François Revel and Matthieu Ricard
books.description: Conversations between Ricard and his father, a leading French thinker, weighing Buddhism against Western philosophy on the big questions of life.
